intro.eyebrow: Aerospace Engineer | Systems and Flight Test
intro.title: Engineering complex
intro.lede: I am Peter Mwaura, an aerospace engineering graduate with a computer science minor focused on propulsion, flight test, systems engineering, and technical leadership. My work spans hybrid-electric VTOL aircraft, AIAA Design/Build/Fly aircraft, high-power rocketry, thermal systems research, wearable haptics, and hands-on manufacturing.

intro.recruiterHeading: I work where analysis, build execution, and operational reality meet.
intro.recruiterBody: This portfolio is built to show how I move from mission intent to engineering evidence. I decompose requirements, model the system, build and instrument prototypes, run tests, interpret the data, and communicate the tradeoffs clearly enough for a team to act.

metrics.label: member team led in AIAA DBF

about.title: Aerospace systems, test evidence, and hardware that has to earn trust.
about.lede: I am most energized by engineering problems that demand rigor across analysis, prototyping, verification, manufacturing, and team coordination. I like turning broad mission goals into requirements, architectures, experiments, and decisions that can survive real operating constraints.
about.workingStyleTitle: I am strongest where analysis, testing, and fabrication have to agree.
workingStyleParagraphs: My strongest work happens in multidisciplinary teams where propulsion, controls, structures, manufacturing, software, and operations all have to connect. I am comfortable contributing at the system level and at the test-bench level, whether that means trade studies, documentation, validation planning, instrumentation, or hands-on build work.

I care a lot about engineering judgment. To me, that means requirements traceability, risk thinking, safety margins, manufacturability, and making sure the design is honest about the environment it has to survive in.

I also bring enough programming background to make analysis and automation useful: MATLAB and Simulink for aircraft and propulsion modeling, Python and C++ for technical computation, SQL and databases for structured data, and Arduino/LabVIEW workflows for sensing, controls, and test support.

about.quote: Good engineering is not just elegant on paper. It survives testing, constraints, and the handoff to the people who have to trust it.
about.quoteBody: That standard shapes how I approach propulsion studies, verification planning, flight operations, manufacturing tradeoffs, safety procedures, and technical communication.

interests.title: I am drawn to engineering where performance has consequences.
interests.lede: The work I keep returning to sits at the intersection of aerospace systems, propulsion, testing, controls, thermal analysis, structures, manufacturing, and mission-driven design. I am especially interested in environments where uncertainty has to be reduced through analysis and disciplined verification.

cards.title: Sizing the aircraft architecture, not just the motor.
cards.description: I am interested in propulsion and power systems where mission energy, voltage/current limits, C-rates, thermal behavior, efficiency losses, and reserve margins shape the architecture.

cards.title: Let the evidence shape the design.
cards.description: I enjoy test plans, instrumentation, calibration, telemetry, wind-tunnel work, thrust characterization, and data reduction workflows that expose what a system is really doing before decisions get locked in.

cards.title: Design choices become real on the shop floor.
cards.description: I like the handoff from CAD and analysis to foam cutting, laser-cut structures, composites, FDM printing, CNC work, assembly, inspection, and repeatable build procedures.

cards.title: Software is strongest when it supports the hardware.
cards.description: My computer science background supports technical computation, sensor-driven prototypes, database thinking, and analysis workflows that make physical tests easier to understand.

favorites: Wind-tunnel, thrust-rig, bench, and flight-test planning
CAD, composites, CNC, 3D printing, and prototype manufacturing
Technical leadership on cross-functional build teams
outsideParagraphs: Outside of class and formal project work, I stay interested in aircraft systems, mission architecture, robotics, data center cooling, recovery systems, avionics packaging, and the practical engineering tradeoffs behind high-performance hardware.

This site is meant to feel closer to a living technical portfolio than a static resume: a place where photos, videos, reports, design reviews, plots, and build documentation can sit beside the engineering decisions behind them.

projects.title: Selected work in propulsion, flight systems, research, manufacturing, and test leadership.
projects.lede: These projects show how I work across system architecture, feasibility analysis, requirements, testing, fabrication, instrumentation, and technical coordination. Each one is framed around the engineering decisions, evidence, and tradeoffs that made the work credible.

items.title: HEART: Hybrid-Electric Aircraft for Rapid Organ Transportation
items.description: Served as Propulsion Lead on a hybrid-electric VTOL UAV intended for rapid organ transportation, translating mission needs into aircraft-level requirements, propulsion architecture, power-management strategy, and testable design assumptions.
bullets: Built MATLAB mission energy and power models across VTOL, hover, cruise, descent, and reserve phases with propulsive efficiency, electrical losses, and design margins included
Performed propulsion and energy-system sizing against battery energy density, voltage/current constraints, C-rating limits, generator output, and high-power transient demands
Showed why an all-electric COTS architecture was not feasible for the mission profile, then helped define a hybrid-electric generator-battery power-sharing architecture
Converted organ-transport mission objectives into engineering targets for range, cruise speed, altitude, reserve power, VTOL capability, endurance, and operating assumptions
Designed low-speed wind-tunnel testing to compare cyclic pitch, collective pitch, and differential thrust control authority in hover and transition regimes
Supported tilt-wing UAV flight testing through stable hover, controlled wing transition, and sustained forward flight
Contributed to fabrication and assembly using CNC foam cutting, laser-cut structural components, and fiberglass composite layup techniques
items.role: Propulsion lead, systems definition, testing and validation

items.title: Competition Aircraft Program Leadership
items.description: Led technical direction for Saint Louis University's AIAA Design/Build/Fly aircraft program, guiding a 30-member team through aircraft configuration, propulsion verification, test readiness, manufacturing, documentation, and competition operations.
bullets: Directed structured design reviews and cross-subsystem technical checkpoints across six teams to track progress, identify risks, and guide configuration decisions
Translated competition rules into quantitative system requirements for weight, power, payload, mission strategy, battery compliance, and performance constraints
Led propulsion trade studies, static thrust characterization, subsystem validation, telemetry review, and pre-flight verification procedures
Performed aircraft constraint analysis of thrust-to-weight ratio and wing loading in MATLAB to support an 18-lbf payload target
Authored and maintained test procedures, manufacturing guidance, and integration documentation to make aircraft builds repeatable
Represented the team at competition through flight operations, troubleshooting, inspections, and technical communication
Expanded active membership by 130 percent and available funding by over 100 percent through recruitment, alumni outreach, proposals, and organizational operations
items.role: President, Chief Engineer, former propulsion and testing lead

items.title: Recovery and Safety Systems for Competitive High-Power Rocketry
items.description: Led recovery and safety work for a Spaceport America Cup high-power rocket program, combining recovery-system modeling, flight validation, composite manufacturing, telemetry testing, avionics integration, documentation, and safety discipline.
bullets: Designed and optimized a parachute recovery system through analytical modeling, ground tests, and flight validation, earning a maximum recovery score at Spaceport America Cup
Co-authored the Groundbreaker technical paper published at AIAA SciTech 2025, consolidating recovery system design, analysis, test results, and flight performance
Developed, implemented, and enforced manufacturing and test safety procedures for energetic-material workflows while maintaining a 100 percent safety record
Fabricated carbon-fiber airframe elements using filament winding to support a high strength-to-weight design for a 10,000-ft target altitude
Validated RF telemetry hardware through range and reliability testing to support post-landing tracking and recovery
Designed and integrated avionics and payload bays for secure electro-mechanical packaging of electronics and recovery hardware
Maintained traceable design analyses, test plans, results, and safety documentation for future team handoff

items.title: Applied Research in Thermal Systems and Haptic Devices
items.description: Worked across data center cooling research and wearable haptics prototyping, using thermodynamic modeling, CAD, circuit development, user testing, Arduino control, and design iteration to improve technical decisions.
bullets: Conducted comparative analysis of data center cooling architectures including air cooling, cold-plate liquid cooling, and immersion cooling from energy and sustainability perspectives
Modeled heat dissipation, coolant selection, mass-flow requirements, rack count, and thermal load behavior through modular thermodynamic analysis
Conceptualized, CAD-modeled, and manufactured wearable haptic prototype components to improve comfort and accessibility
Validated designs through three user-test cycles with 10 plus participants, reducing donning time by 48 percent and reducing form factor by 40 percent
Developed electronic circuits from schematic capture through breadboard and perfboard prototyping, then bench-tested for signal integrity and function
Programmed Arduino control logic for piezo sensor input and vibration motor feedback, achieving 95 percent detection accuracy across 20 plus trials
